summary: Pocahontas County, WV former tower completed by the state forestry division in the 1920s; 1926 telephone link; site now a public overlook with boardwalk, no remains described.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the tower Gone; Mon Forest Towns calls it a former tower and describes no remains

access.note: The overlook and boardwalk are a public roadside stop on the Highland Scenic Highway; the sources do not say anything about access to the tower site itself

visit.trail_note: Quarter-mile accessible boardwalk from the Big Spruce Overlook parking area; the guide describes no remains of the tower

events.note: Mon Forest Towns says the WV Division of Forestry completed the tower in the 1920s; year shown is the start of that decade, not a known build year
October 1926 Charleston Gazette item: telephone connection to the central offices at Marlinton and Richwood
Forest Service marker: a fire on the cut-over spruce land in 1930, probably set by train cinders; no source ties this fire to the tower
Registered January 26, 2017, nominated by Brian M. Powell

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 4,548 ft (1,386 m) for the site; the Forest Service marker gives a site elevation of 4,520 ft. The register figure is kept because it matches the brief; the difference is 28 ft and the sources do not say which point each figure refers to.

sources.title: Black Mountain Tower Site

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: coordinates, registration date, gone status and elevation match the register; no corrections. The site is a public roadside overlook with a boardwalk, but no source describes the tower site itself or its access. The 1926 telephone note comes from a reprinted Charleston Gazette item, not the original. The 1930 fire is from a Forest Service marker and is not tied to the tower anywhere in the sources, so it is kept only as context in the story. The marker's 4,520 ft site elevation differs from the register's 4,548 ft.
